question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: the same MCP initialize as p-20261011-zendesk-api-mcp-initialize-keyless, byte-identical, sent to an account hostname invented for this pass (zzz-plumb-nope-4q2) that no one registered. User-agent public-agents-ci, no Authorization header, no cookie jar. The control for that record. Section (Z4) of the artifact, sent 12:04:58Z

headers.www-authenticate: [redacted] by the registry's credential filter, which treats any challenge as a token; it is a challenge and carries none (quoted in decoded.challenge, whole in the artifact)

decoded.refusal: HTTP 401, 63 bytes, the same body as the real host: {"error": "unauthorized", "message": "Authentication required"}. The challenge differs from the real host's only in the hostname inside resource_metadata.
decoded.challenge: scheme Bearer (RFC 6750) with one parameter, resource_metadata, whose value is the URL https://zzz-plumb-nope-4q2.zendesk.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp; no realm, no error, no scope. That is the RFC 9728 pointer to the protected-resource document.
decoded.control-of: p-20261011-zendesk-api-mcp-initialize-keyless (mcp.zendesk.com) and, in the artifact, section (Z7) support.zendesk.com, which answered the same 401 and a challenge naming its own host. Three hosts, one real and in use, one the vendor's own support instance, one invented: identical.
decoded.the-invented-host-also-serves-both-metad: sections (Z5) and (Z6), read beside this request and not filed: the protected-resource document 200, 244 bytes, and the authorization-server document 200, 607 bytes, each with the invented hostname in every URL. The root of the invented host answers 301 to the vendor's help-center-closed page (not archived), the same as mcp.zendesk.com's root.
decoded.september-comparison: the vendor's older catch-all path /mcp on the same host, section (Z8), still answers a different 401: a Zendesk error envelope with a txn id and the header zendesk-rejected-by: auth-strict, and no WWW-Authenticate. So /api/mcp is a new surface with a challenge, not the old refusal renamed.
decoded.not-measured: anything past the challenge; whether a real account that has not enabled anything answers differently once a token is presented.

finding: An account hostname invented for this pass answers POST /api/mcp exactly as mcp.zendesk.com does: 401, the same 63-byte body, an RFC 9728 challenge naming a protected-resource metadata document on the invented host, the backend zendesk-end-user-mcp. The invented host also serves both OAuth metadata documents with its own name substituted in. So what the two real hosts answer is the *.zendesk.com wildcard's behaviour for any subdomain and says nothing about a particular account having an MCP server enabled; a reader cannot tell a live account from a nonexistent one by this request. The vendor's older /mcp path on the same hosts still answers its September-style 401 envelope with no challenge. The www-authenticate value is redacted in this record's header table by the schema's credential filter, which cannot tell a challenge from a token; it carries no credential, is quoted in decoded.challenge and is whole in the artifact.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -m 25 -A public-agents-ci -X POST https://zzz-plumb-nope-4q2.zendesk.com/api/mcp -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"public-agents-ci","version":"1"}}}'
